title: fix(lint): the translation rule's OBJECT rung reads what the artifact's packages[] provide
body:
Fixes #19064

`translation-target-unknown`'s OBJECT rung built its universe from `stack.objects` alone while this rule's own docblock already declared the wider reach `validateObjectReferences`' `artifactProvidedObjectNames` uses. The declaration and the implementation disagreed inside one file, and on `os build`'s per-package leg the author paid for it.

Clause-②: no

## The measurement, re-taken on `origin/main` before anything was touched

PR #19060 rewrote this very file on 2026-09-20, so the card's premise was re-measured first-hand at `74fb2f7a80` rather than inherited. Every reading below is a PRINT of every hit, never a count:

```
$ git grep -n -E 'stack\.objects|manifest\.objects' -- packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts
:752   * registry merges the layers. So a universe built from `stack.objects` alone
:851  for (const obj of recordsOf(stack.objects)) {      ← the OBJECT rung's only universe

⇒ `manifest.objects`: ZERO hits. The query asks for BOTH tokens, so the absence is a reading.

LIT CONTROL — same query form, same corpus, the rule that already closed this shape:
$ git grep -n 'artifactProvidedObjectNames' -- packages/lint/src/
validate-object-references.ts:163      function artifactProvidedObjectNames(stack: AnyRec)
validate-object-references.ts:210      for (const n of artifactProvidedObjectNames(stack)) resolvable.add(n);
validate-translation-references.ts:692 the docblock that CLAIMS the reach — and nothing that implements it
```

⇒ the instrument finds the token where it exists, so its absence in the translation rule is a reading and not a dark grep.

**The diagnostic, re-run rather than relayed** (the probe is `examples/app-multi-package`'s shape: `core` owns `crm_account`, `orders` translates it, judged on the per-package leg `packageBodyAsStack(body, entries)` builds):

```
translations[0]["zh-CN"].objects.crm_account   error · translation-target-unknown
  Translations are keyed to "crm_account", which no object in this stack defines. The
  resolver looks up keys derived from the metadata, so this whole subtree is dead weight …
  Rename the key to the object it was written for, drop it, or ignore this if the object is
  contributed by another installed package. Defined objects: crm_order.
```

That is the remedy that deletes a translation the runtime resolves, at `error`, so the run FAILS on it — and it is byte-identical, but for the name, to what a genuine typo yields on the same stack.

⚠️ The card body still carries `Blocked-by: #18442`. Re-taken here: #18441 and #18442 read `closed` / `completed` and #19060 landed as `6f8d751bc1`. The line is stale; it is not a reason to stop.

## The precedent — followed, and the judgement the card asked for

`validateObjectReferences` closed this exact shape on this exact carrier for object NAMES (#16611). **It cannot be reused as-is, and the difference is the RETURN, not the reach**:

| | `artifactProvidedObjectNames` (#16611) | `artifactProvidedObjects` (here) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| carrier | `packages[].manifest.objects` | the same, unchanged |
| entry shape | ADR-0130 D4 `{ manifest: body }`, no readable body contributes nothing | the same |
| returns | `string[]` — that rule asks only whether a reference RESOLVES | the RECORDS — this universe is keyed by FACTS (the fields, options, views, sections and rules a key may address beneath `objects.NAME`) |

A name-only fold here would resolve the object key and then judge the owner's own field keys against an EMPTY fact set — reporting every one of them as an orphan, which is the same false positive one level up and the mistake `objectExtensionsByTarget` records for a target it cannot see. A wholesale subtree SKIP (rung 2b's answer) is wrong for the opposite reason: rung 2b skips because the owner's field set is genuinely invisible from a package that only EXTENDS the target, whereas a sibling's declaration is fully readable here — skipping would leave the per-package leg unable to see a typo the union leg reports. So the records are folded through the SAME collector the declaration loop uses, and the subtree stays judged.

Where both the stack in hand and a sibling declare the same field or action name, the record this leg is JUDGING keeps the slot: which layer's `options` a merged field carries is the registry's precedence question, and `checkOptionKeys` is the only consumer of the stored definition — the same decision the `objectExtensions` fold took one collection over.

## Both control directions, pinned side by side

A false-positive fix without a false-NEGATIVE control is the shape this repo keeps carding, so every pin below is in the same describe block as the acceptance it neighbours:

| direction | pin |
|:--|:--|
| the false orphan is gone | the sibling-declared object key, and its field / option / `_validations` keys, resolve |
| ⭐ CONTROL — the context is what does the work | the same bundle, the same package judged ALONE, still errors |
| ⭐ NON-DEGENERACY | a name NO entry of the artifact declares is still `error`, and the remedy now enumerates what the artifact provides (`Defined objects: crm_account, crm_order.`) |
| ⭐ NON-DEGENERACY, one rung down | a field the sibling does not declare is still `error` under the now-resolved object (`Declared fields: industry, name.`) |
| both on ONE bundle | a sibling key beside a typo reports exactly the typo |
| the widening is not a path | an entry with no readable body (a segment reference) makes nothing addressable |
| no collateral widening | the single-`defineStack` shape is untouched — `objects` is a STACK collection, so there is no `stack.manifest.objects` form to read |

## Reverse verification, from the COMMITTED fix

`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` deleted the fold's two call lines and ran the file's suite, with the mutation proved on disk rather than by an exit code:

```
anchor x1 -> x0 · blob 21d35a8b8de4 -> 7995be70fa39      (the mutation LANDED)
Tests  5 failed | 100 passed (105)                       (the expected direction: RED)
restore: blob after restore == blob at HEAD (21d35a8b8de4) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

All five reds are the new pins — the acceptances AND both non-degeneracy controls, whose hint assertions are themselves non-vacuous.

## Checks — real exit codes

| command | exit |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build` (dependency closure) | **0** |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` — 106 files, 4000 passed / 5 skipped | **0** |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` (incl. `check:test-typecheck`) | **0** |
| `pnpm lint` (repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`) | **0** |
| 53 of the 57 families `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derives for this diff | **0** each |
| `pnpm check:docs-transcript-drift` — re-run after `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint...' build`, since it derives from the BUILT registry | **0** |

⊘ NOT MEASURED locally, declared to CI — each exited **3**, which these gates define as "nothing was measured", neither a pass nor a finding: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` and `check:type-check-debt` all refuse without a whole-repo `pnpm build`. The artifact-roster and whole-tree families the derivation prints as unplaceable are CI's runs, not this PR's.

## Acceptance notes

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`'s key table still describes `objects.{object}` as "an object this stack defines, or a platform object". That row already understated the universe after #18441 added the `objectExtensions[]` target rung and nothing updated it; it is a doc completeness nit on a page this PR does not touch, noted rather than filed, and the next rung card on this rule is the natural carrier.
